topic: ISS-3113 Chapman-1933 cross-surface patch set (30 exact-text patches) - pre-integration citation/wording review
current_verdict_holds_note: No verdict changes are proposed and none are recommended. The patch set touches prose only. The frozen predictions/eclipse-2026-08-12-predictions.json is not touched (confirmed: not a target_file in any patch).
our_argument_summary: The analyst (ISS-3113-chapman-cross-surface-findings.json:prose_patches) proposes 30 exact-text patches. They re-describe Chapman (1933) as a theoretical treatment whose author judged the then-available eclipse records did not show the effect, withdraw the unsourced 5-25 / 5-30 nT range from 12+ surfaces, annotate the §4.2.6 pre-commitment (P13), and fix the bibliography venue mix-up (P24). In place of the range, the patches argue non-discrimination from "the dome's magnitudes are the 2017 Boulder measurement rescaled by coverage" (ISS-3113-chapman-cross-surface-findings.json:kernel_of_truth).

per_patch.note: Removes "Chapman 1933 explains it". Neutral, correct.

Kim & Chang 2018 (ASR 61:2040) confirm an averaged eclipse geomagnetic signal, not the Sq mechanism. Write "a known eclipse effect on the Sq currents (worked out by Chapman in 1933; a statistically confirmed eclipse signal in INTERMAGNET data, Kim & Chang 2018)". See H3.

Matches the Crossref abstract (Chapman 1933): no regular effect of the predicted type; "a final decision must await further observations". "did not yet show it" is a fair gloss. Optional: add that Chapman drew the (later superseded) inference that Sq is probably not in the E-layer (H5).
"worked out theoretically by Chapman in 1933 and confirmed in observatory data since" stays within both sources (an eclipse signal is what was confirmed).
Same mechanism-vs-signal attribution as P02 (H3). Otherwise good: TLDR stays correct and the 3.6x point is unchanged.
Correct and no number needed: Meza 2022 shows sign and size depend on station and component.

Priority claim "first worked out by Chapman (1933)" is not supported by the source, and Bauer (1901/1902) had already attributed the eclipse magnetic effect to an upper-atmosphere change. Drop "first", or say "the first quantitative E-layer treatment". Citation (TME 38(3):175-183) verified. See H4.

Verified against the Kim & Chang (2018) ASR abstract: 207 records, 100 observatories, 39 eclipses, 1991-2016. "roughly 200" is fair. Suggest exact counts (207 / 100 / 39) to pre-empt the WIN-068 confusion (H7).

Verified: Meza, Bosch, Natali & Eylenstein (2022) ASR 69(1):16-25, doi 10.1016/j.asr.2021.07.029. The arXiv:2107.12327 abstract contains "strikingly accurately", with an Ashour-Chapman approximation fed by GNSS TEC depletion. Figure-read BOU dX/dZ values are labelled approximate. NOTE: this patch is correct, and it is what makes H1 visible: it says Boulder Z was small and positive, while P11/P12/P15/P21/P22/P23/P26/P27 call -10.9 nT "the 2017 Boulder measurement".
No quantity needed; correct.

"the window is itself the 2017 Boulder measurement rescaled by coverage" presents the dome's -10.9 nT as a Boulder measurement of the eclipse effect. Replace with "the window is the dome's BOU-2017 baseline (-10.9 nT, an imported figure the dome does not tie to a stated baseline; see WIN-010) rescaled by coverage".

"the 2017 Boulder value (-10.9 nT) ... so any coverage-scaled standard treatment fit to the same past observations lands in the same place" is unsupported. WIN-010 (c18-approved) finds quiet-day-referenced Boulder Z at eclipse maximum of +0.3 to +4.9 nT, "never near the dome's -10.9 nT". A standard treatment fitted to Boulder Z would not land at -10.9. Keep the withdrawal of 5-25 nT and the second sentence; replace the first with "are the dome's BOU-2017 baseline (-10.9 nT) multiplied by coverage and FSF - an imported magnitude, not one derived from dome geometry (see WIN-010 and §4.2.5)".

Annotated, not rewritten. The commitment sentence and the 25/26.2 nT window that follows stay byte-identical; the note is dated and says we evaluate against it as written. This is the correct pattern for a post-event fix to a pre-commitment.

TLDR: "the dome's magnitudes are a rescaled 2017 Boulder measurement, so they cannot discriminate" carries both H1 and H2 into the most-read surface. Suggested: "...already predicts an eclipse magnetic signal, and the dome's magnitudes are imported from a single 2017 Boulder figure rather than derived from dome geometry."
"the 2017 Boulder observation rescaled ... a globe-Earth measurement of the ionospheric Sq-current effect": same defect as P11. Use the imported-baseline wording.

"reproduces the same per-station numbers" goes further than §4.2.5 point 4, which supports a shared arithmetic FORM (amplitude x coverage x station weight), not the same numbers. Write "has the same arithmetic form (see §4.2.5)".
"the Sq-current mechanism ... confirmed statistically by Kim & Chang 2018": the paper confirms a signal and does not test the mechanism. Otherwise good.
Both cited papers document eclipse perturbations. Correct.
"first worked out theoretically": same priority problem as P07. The DOI swap from Wikipedia to 10.1029/TE038i003p00175 is good.
Verified against the ASR abstract. Suggest exact counts, as for P08.
TLDR "the 2017 Boulder measurement rescaled by coverage, so it matches what a standard Sq-current treatment of the same data gives": same as P12, on a TLDR surface.
"the 2017 Boulder measurement of that same effect": H1. "Sq-current mechanism ... confirmed statistically": H3.
"a coverage-rescaled 2017 globe-Earth measurement of the standard Sq-current effect": H1.

All four entries verified on Crossref this run: Chapman 1919 (Phil Trans A 218:1-118, doi 10.1098/rsta.1919.0001); Chapman 1933 (TME 38(3):175-183, title matches); Kim & Chang 2018 (ASR 61(8):2040-2049, Jung-Hee Kim & Heon-Young Chang); Meza et al. 2022 (ASR 69(1):16-25; four authors correct). Fixes the venue mix-up. If the H6 follow-up fixes attribution, also add Kim & Chang 2018 JKAS 51(4):119-127, doi 10.5303/JKAS.2018.51.4.119.
Good. Minor H3: the parenthetical attaches "confirmed statistically" to the mechanism; prefer "an eclipse signal confirmed statistically".

"The dome's magnitudes are the 2017 Boulder measurement (-10.9 nT) rescaled ... a standard Sq-current treatment of the same data gives the same numbers; the magnitude test cannot discriminate." H1 (it is not the standard-processed Boulder value) and H2 (a result-independent "cannot discriminate" on a kill-shot while the eclipse magnetic verdict is still pending).

Keep the useful second half (timing / component-sign pattern as the real discriminator). Replace "the band is a coverage-rescaled globe-Earth measurement" with "the band's magnitude is imported, not derived".
"worked out ... in 1933" and "The 0 nT claim is false" are both supported.
Supported.
Good use of Chapman 1919 for Sq and 1933 for eclipses. "confirmed statistically by Kim & Chang 2018" attached to the mechanism: same as H3.

holes_found.description: The replacement argument presents the dome's -10.9 nT BOU-2017 baseline as "the 2017 Boulder measurement/observation" and "a globe-Earth measurement of the ionospheric Sq-current effect", and concludes that a standard treatment of the same data gives the same numbers. Our own c18-approved WIN-010 says the opposite (data/wins.json:WIN-010.detail_evidence): quiet-day-referenced Boulder Z at eclipse maximum is +0.3 to +4.9 nT under every variant, "never near the dome's -10.9 nT"; "The dome's figures come from its choice of baseline. It does not say which baseline gives -10.9 nT"; and the dome's own OPEN-009 re-audit gives -18.22 nT. P09 in this same patch set says Boulder Z was "small and positive (a few nT)" (Meza et al. 2022, Fig. 7). Applied as written, §4.2.2 would say Boulder Z was positive while §4.2.3, §5 Test 5, §6.4, §8.11, §9.2 and KS-005 call -10.9 nT the Boulder measurement of that effect. That is an internal contradiction any careful reader finds by expanding WIN-010. The source the analyst points to does not rescue it: §4.2.5 point 1 (data/sections.json:part4.html#p4-425) still calls -10.9 nT "a Chapman-mechanism measurement on a spherical Earth" (a pre-existing defect the patch set copies onto seven new surfaces), and §4.2.5 point 4 supports only a shared arithmetic FORM, not shared numbers. Other side, for fairness: -10.9 nT is plausibly a real reading of the Boulder record under some unstated baseline that does not remove the diurnal Sq swing, so "measurement" is not fabricated. "Measurement of the Sq-current eclipse effect" is what is wrong.
holes_found.recommendation: Rev2: in every listed patch, describe -10.9 nT as the dome's BOU-2017 baseline, an imported figure the dome does not tie to a stated baseline and which our WIN-010 analysis cannot reproduce as an eclipse effect. Make the non-discrimination point as "the magnitude is imported from observation, not derived from dome geometry" plus "same arithmetic form (§4.2.5 point 4)". Drop "a standard treatment of the same data gives the same numbers / reproduces the same per-station numbers / lands in the same place". File a follow-up to fix the §4.2.5 point 1 and part8 "a real INTERMAGNET observation" wording so that it matches WIN-010.

holes_found.description: Several replacements newly state a result-independent "the magnitude test cannot discriminate" on the kill-shot card and on TLDRs. The eclipse magnetic verdict (PRED-095 / TIER-1 / TIER-3 / R005) is still pending (EXP-687 rev6 pending per monitor/curmudgeon/reviews/ECLIPSE-2026-08-12-MAGNETIC-RESULTS-proposal.c5.json:operator_decisions.decision_1_symmetric_labelling). If standard physics expects near-zero or positive Z at Boulder-like stations (WIN-010; Meza 2022), then a one-signed -5 to -26 nT band is at least partly discriminable, which is exactly what the results draft is weighing. Hard-coding "cannot discriminate" on KS-005 now would pre-empt that decision. The other side: §4.2.5 point 4 already argued non-discrimination before the event, so this is not a new position. But it argued it from the shared arithmetic form, and these patches restate it as a property of the numbers, which relies on C1-1.
holes_found.recommendation: Keep the non-discrimination claim on these surfaces at the structural level ("imported magnitude; same arithmetic form; see §4.2.5"), or point to §4.2.5 instead of restating a conclusion. Revisit the KS-005 wording when the operator settles the eclipse labelling.

holes_found.description: Kim & Chang 2018 (Adv. Space Res. 61(8):2040-2049) are cited as confirming "the Sq-current mechanism". Their abstract (KNU repository, read this run) reports a statistical average over 207 records from 100 observatories during 39 eclipses (1991-2016): an increase in Y and decreases in X and F within about 180 min of maximum, often overwhelmed by daily geomagnetic activity. The effect "has proved subtle to be detected". The paper confirms an eclipse geomagnetic SIGNAL. It does not test or name the mechanism. This is the "says no more than the source" check in the HNOTE focus. Not critical: the Sq mechanism is standard (Yamazaki & Maute 2017), but the attribution belongs to the theory literature, not to K&C.
holes_found.recommendation: Rephrase as "an eclipse geomagnetic signal confirmed statistically across INTERMAGNET (Kim & Chang 2018)" and leave mechanism attribution to Chapman 1919/1933 and Yamazaki & Maute 2017. Consider adding K&C's own "subtle to be detected" caveat where we discuss size; it helps our honesty and costs nothing.

holes_found.description: "The eclipse mechanism was first worked out by Chapman (1933)" and "first worked out theoretically" are priority claims that neither source makes. Bauer (1901, 1902; Nature 64:16, 65:246) had already attributed the eclipse magnetic effect to a change in the upper atmosphere caused by the loss of sunlight, about 30 years earlier, though qualitatively. monitor/curmudgeon/alerts.txt (2026-10-04, WIN-010.c18) already flagged "Chapman 'first proposed' wording" (moderate). The same defect class is now being reintroduced on two more surfaces.
holes_found.recommendation: Drop "first". "Chapman (1933) worked out the E-layer Sq-current version of this effect quantitatively" is safe.

holes_found.description: "(he judged that the eclipse records of his day did not yet show it)" is accurate but leaves out the inference Chapman actually drew from the null: that Sq is "probably not produced in the E-layer" (the Crossref abstract). Later work placed the Sq dynamo in the E-region, so Chapman's 1933 inference was wrong in direction. A defender who reads the abstract could say our founding citation argued against the mechanism we credit to it.
holes_found.recommendation: Optional, one clause in the §4.2.2 detail (P08): "...and inferred, provisionally, that Sq is probably not an E-layer current, a conclusion later work reversed."

holes_found.description: Two pre-commitments outside §4.2.6 lose their referent. part9 still reads "We commit publicly: if August 2026 measurements fall in the W004 range but outside the Chapman mechanism's expected range...", and part4 has a sister "(a) the measured anomalies fall within the W004 baseline predictions but outside the Chapman mechanism's expected range" sentence. Once P12/P23 remove the 5-25 nT range, "the Chapman mechanism's expected range" is defined nowhere except the annotated §4.2.6 25 nT figure. The commitments are correctly left unrewritten. But a reader can no longer tell what range they commit to.
holes_found.recommendation: Add a dated pointer annotation (not a rewrite) after each: "[Note added October 2026: the range this commitment refers to is the one stated in §4.2.6, evaluated as written; see the note there.]"

hnote_focus_answers.focus_1_citations: Verified directly this run. Chapman 1933: Crossref doi 10.1029/TE038i003p00175; title "The effect of a solar eclipse on the Earth's magnetic field", TME 38(3):175-183, Sept 1933; the abstract supports the "judged the observations showed no regular effect; final decision must await further observations" wording. Kim & Chang 2018: Crossref doi 10.1016/j.asr.2018.01.022; "Statistical analysis of geomagnetic field variations during solar eclipses", ASR 61(8):2040-2049; abstract read via the KNU repository (207 records / 100 observatories / 39 eclipses / 1991-2016; Y up, X and F down; no latitude band, no Z, no mechanism). Also verified: Chapman 1919 (doi 10.1098/rsta.1919.0001, Phil Trans A 218:1-118) and Meza et al. 2022 (doi 10.1016/j.asr.2021.07.029; arXiv:2107.12327 abstract contains "strikingly accurately"). The patches say no more than the sources, EXCEPT C1-3 (mechanism attributed to K&C) and C1-4 ("first").
hnote_focus_answers.focus_2_quantitative_gaps: Partly. Removing 5-25 nT leaves the §4.2.6 commitment self-contained (it carries its own 25 nT figure, now annotated). It leaves the part9 commitment and the part4 "(a)" commitment without a defined range (C1-6). The replacement support (§4.2.5) does NOT support each place it replaces: point 4 supports a shared arithmetic form, while point 1's "Chapman-mechanism measurement" framing of -10.9 nT conflicts with WIN-010 and with P09 (C1-1). Places where the substitute claim goes beyond §4.2.5: P12, P14, P15, P16, P21, P22, P23, P26.
hnote_focus_answers.focus_4_out_of_scope: File ONE follow-up ISS, but with a different scope from the one the analyst proposed. (a) WIN-025: yes. "5-30 nT" unsourced (detail_evidence, detail_verdict_text, tldr_evidence); "first explained by Chapman (1919)" / "known since Chapman (1919)" attributes eclipse work to the Sq paper; "statistical analyses across dozens of eclipses (Curto et al., 2006)" is unverified. (b) WIN-068 "39 eclipses": NOT a defect. Kim & Chang's ASR abstract states "207 geomagnetic manifestations acquired by 100 geomagnetic observatories during 39 solar eclipses occurring from 1991 to 2016", so the analyst's suspected conflation is wrong; drop that sub-item. (c) NEW and more important: the 30-50 deg magnetic-latitude band, "grows with eclipse magnitude" and "decreases in X, Z and F" come from a DIFFERENT paper, Kim & Chang (2018), J. Korean Astron. Soc. 51(4):119-127, doi 10.5303/JKAS.2018.51.4.119 (abstract read this run). The ASR paper's abstract has no latitude band and no Z. WIN-010 (detail_evidence and the pre-registered magnetic-latitude profile in detail_verdict_text), WIN-068 (detail_verdict_text "X/Z/F decreases at magnetic latitudes 30-50") and this patch set's own source_checks.kim_chang_2018 note all attribute these findings to ASR 61:2040. That would be the fifth citation failure in this cluster (H6).

stronger_arguments.description: Use the imported-magnitude argument, which needs no claim about what -10.9 nT physically is: the dome's eclipse magnitude enters as a number taken from observation (BOU 2017, later re-audited by the dome itself to -18.22 nT) and is not derived from disc radius, firmament height or any dome parameter. That point is fully sourced in WIN-010 and survives whichever way the eclipse labelling goes.

Cite Kim & Chang's own caveat that the eclipse effect "has proved subtle to be detected" and can be overwhelmed by daily geomagnetic activity. That is an honest statement about size that replaces the withdrawn 5-25 nT range without inventing a number.

kernel_of_truth.description: The analyst's core correction is right and overdue. Chapman (1933) gave no 5-25 nT figure and judged that the eclipse records then available showed no regular effect of the predicted type (Crossref abstract, doi 10.1029/TE038i003p00175). The part10 bibliography did attach Chapman 1919's Phil Trans A 218:1-118 venue to the 1933 paper (data/sections.json:part10.html#p10-2; fixed by P24, all four entries verified). The §4.2.6 pre-commitment is annotated, not rewritten (ISS-3113-chapman-cross-surface-findings.json:prose_patches[P13]).
kernel_of_truth.why_it_doesnt_save_claim: The substitute argument swaps one untraced number for an overstated description of another. -10.9 nT is the dome's BOU-2017 baseline. Our own WIN-010 finds that standard-processed Boulder Z at eclipse maximum is positive and "never near the dome's -10.9 nT" (data/wins.json:WIN-010.detail_evidence), and P09 in this same set says Boulder Z was small and positive (ISS-3113-chapman-cross-surface-findings.json:prose_patches[P09]). Calling it "the Boulder measurement of the Sq effect" on ten surfaces creates the internal contradiction a defender would use.

recommended_action_note: REVISE before integration: rev2 of the patch set, not a WIN verdict change. 17 patches can stand as written (P01, P03, P04, P06, P08, P09, P10, P13, P18, P20, P24, P28, P29; P25 with a minor wording tweak; plus P02, P05 and P30, which need only the C1-3 one-phrase fix). The C1-1 cluster (P11, P12, P14, P15, P16, P21, P22, P23, P26, P27) needs its replacement rationale rewritten, and P07/P19 need "first" removed. Integrate as one set after rev2, not piecemeal: applying P09 alone would add a "Boulder Z positive" statement next to the existing §4.2.5 "Chapman-mechanism measurement" wording. Re-review of rev2 can be verification class if C1-1..C1-6 are applied as written.
deeper_analysis: Which way do the holes cut? C1-1 and C1-2 are on our side: they stop us claiming more than our own WIN-010 analysis supports, and stop us pre-judging a pending eclipse verdict in a direction that happens to suit neither labelling cleanly. A dome defender would actually welcome "-10.9 nT is a real Boulder measurement", because it makes the dome's baseline look empirically grounded. The objection comes from the other direction, a careful critic or an independent geophysicist, who would see that we called the same Boulder record both positive and -10.9 nT. C1-3 and C1-4 are standard over-citation that a defender can exploit cheaply ("your source doesn't say that"). The cluster's history (four prior citation failures, now a possible fifth via the JKAS/ASR venue mix) argues for verifying every abstract before integration, which is why this review read both K&C abstracts and Crossref records directly instead of carrying the WIN-010 description forward.

summary_for_decider: HNOTE commission (no queue_id). ISS-3113 Chapman cross-surface patch set: REVISE (rev2) before integration. 17 of 30 patches can stand as written or with a one-phrase fix. Major C1-1: ten replacements call the dome's -10.9 nT "the 2017 Boulder measurement of the Sq effect", which contradicts c18-approved WIN-010 (Boulder Z at maximum +0.3 to +4.9 nT, "never near -10.9") and P09 in the same set. Moderates: C1-2 ("cannot discriminate" on KS-005/TLDRs pre-judges the pending eclipse verdict), C1-3 (K&C confirm a signal, not the mechanism), C1-4 ("first worked out": Bauer 1901), C1-6 (part9/part4 commitments lose their range referent; annotate). P13 confirmed annotate-only. Citations verified directly. Follow-up ISS recommended: the K&C 30-50 deg band is from JKAS 51(4):119, not ASR (WIN-010, WIN-068, eclipse pre-registration), plus WIN-025. WIN-068 "39 eclipses" is CORRECT; drop the analyst's suspicion. Do not integrate piecemeal.
